Recommendation: 1. Record the exact time of every GRAP order
Finding it rests on and its status: H2 is INCONCLUSIVE: the hour of the stage change is uncertain for 27 of 30 changes and 'assumed' for 11; the 12-hour buffer is needed because of it (data gap)
What we are not claiming: that GRAP does or does not lower PM2.5
Action: Publish the date and hour of each invocation and revocation with the order; keep one machine-readable log
Indicator and target: share of stage changes with a documented hour; proposed target 100%
Data needed: order timestamps and the stage in force by hour

Recommendation: 2. Build a design that can test H2
Finding it rests on and its status: one event can only detect a fall of at least 48%; about 17 events are needed for a 15% fall, against 1 qualifying event per winter (frozen result: H2 INCONCLUSIVE)
What we are not claiming: that a modest effect of GRAP is absent
Action: Do not draw policy conclusions about GRAP from one city and one winter; extend over several winters and add a paired or staggered comparison (several cities, or stations outside the NCR with their own record)
Responsible stakeholder: CAQM with state boards and an academic partner
Timeline: design before winter 2027-28; collect over 2027-28 and 2028-29
Indicator and target: number of events with a usable counterfactual (hold-out error at most 25%); proposed target at least 3, then the number in T11a
Data needed: PM2.5, weather and stage by hour for the comparison cities for several winters

Recommendation: 3. Put monitors and smoke estimates where the fires are
Finding it rests on and its status: H1 is WEAKLY SUPPORTED (frozen rule met): the association is mostly between months (day-to-day part +3.4%, interval -2.8% to +10.1%) and fire adds 1.8 points of R-squared beyond weather; the stations are in Delhi-NCR, Patna, Lucknow and Kanpur, none in the main burning districts of Punjab and Haryana (exploratory extension)
What we are not claiming: that fires cause a given share of Delhi's PM2.5, or anything about a single state
Action: Add PM2.5 monitors in the main burning districts and use fire radiative power or smoke estimates, not counts alone, before setting fire-season targets
Indicator and target: number of PM2.5 stations in the burning districts; proposed target: at least one per district with frequent fires
Data needed: PM2.5 near the fires, fire radiative power, several burning seasons

Finding it rests on and its status: the winter sample has 424 network-outage hours and 84.7% valid station-hours; up to 242 outage hours fall within 7 days of one stage change (data gap)
What we are not claiming: that the air was clean while stations were silent
Action: Treat outage hours as a reported KPI and fix the networks that drop out in the burning season
Indicator and target: share of valid station-hours from October to February; proposed target at least 90% (now 84.7%)
Data needed: outage log by station and hour

Recommendation: 5. Use a simple persistence-based advisory, and monitor it
Finding it rests on and its status: on unseen days, yesterday's PM2.5 plus weather gives an RMSE of 23.4 ug/m3 against 43.9 for weather only and 43.0 with fire; 95% of winter days are above 60 ug/m3 (exploratory extension)
What we are not claiming: that this is a validated forecast: it rests on one winter and misses cold extremes
Action: Base next-day advisories on yesterday's level and weather, re-check the error every month against the drift flags of F16
Timeline: pilot this winter (2026-27), review before winter 2027-28
Indicator and target: monthly RMSE of the persistence-plus-weather model against 1.5 times its own training RMSE (30.2 ug/m3), an alarm level of 45 ug/m3; January 2026 (51 ug/m3) would be flagged (months above it: 2026-01); proposed: no unflagged month
Data needed: daily PM2.5 by city and the weather forecast

Recommendation: 6. Treat the Diwali week as its own high-risk window
Finding it rests on and its status: the activation of 19 Oct 2025 (Stage 1 to 2, in the days before Diwali) shows +273% against its counterfactual and the control cities show +262% on the same date, so the rise is shared and is not a result of the stage; with the festival periods controlled the fire association is +9.0% per +5 detections against +9.5% without (exploratory extension)
What we are not claiming: that fireworks, or the stage, explain the rise
Action: Plan advisories and enforcement for the Diwali week separately from other activations, and do not read a rise in that week as a failure of a stage
Indicator and target: PM2.5 in the festival window against the weeks around it, reported every year
Data needed: festival dates, hourly PM2.5, firework rules and their enforcement

Finding it rests on and its status: in January 2026 the weather-and-fire model's error was 2.3 times its training RMSE and the input with the largest drift was temperature (KS 0.55); the model had not seen weather that cold (monitoring result)
What we are not claiming: that the model is wrong in normal weather
Action: When the monthly mean temperature leaves the range of the training period, treat model forecasts as unreliable and rely on the latest observed level
Indicator and target: months flagged by the temperature drift test before the error rises; proposed: every cold spell flagged

Recommendation: 8. Monitor fires out to 200 km, not only 100 km upwind
Finding it rests on and its status: the all-direction count within 200 km is associated with +24.2% per SD (interval +14.8% to +34.4%) against +9.5% for the upwind 100 km count (exploratory extension)
What we are not claiming: that fires beyond 200 km, or in a given state, explain Delhi's PM2.5
Action: Include fire counts out to 200 km in fire-season monitoring and in the monitors proposed in recommendation 3
Indicator and target: daily 200 km counts available for every station; proposed: complete
Data needed: satellite fire detections and station wind

Recommendation: 9. Check siting and calibration of the stations that sit highest and lowest, and read PM2.5 as a regional level
Finding it rests on and its status: stations differ from the regional level by a stable amount (-31% to +31%; H4 SUPPORTED) and 42% of that spread lies between network owners
What we are not claiming: that a high station has a local source rather than an instrument offset
Action: Compare nearby or co-located reference monitors across networks and describe the siting of the highest and lowest stations before any enforcement decision; use regional levels, not single stations, for advisories
Indicator and target: share of stations with a documented siting and calibration check; proposed target 100%
Data needed: siting descriptions and calibration records for each station
